The tenth beta of CoSky 8.0, still for developers to try. It fixes copying in a Dashboard served over plain HTTP, which could lose a token just made, and brings agent skills for connecting applications and for moving from 6.x. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

There is no compatibility promise before `8.0.0-rc.1`, which freezes what [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning) lists. Nothing an application or a deployment sees changes from beta.9.

## Try it

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes: a server in development mode, a Spring Boot application that reads a Config and registers, and another that finds it.

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0-beta.10 --dev
```

What helps most is still what we could only try on one machine: Redis Sentinel or Cluster of your own with a failover, an OIDC provider other than Keycloak, moving a 6.x installation with `cosky-migrate`, and a real network. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you.

## New

- **Agent skills.** `skills/` holds two skills for coding agents, published in the [Ahoo-Wang skills marketplace](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/skills) as `ahoo-cosky-skills` for Claude Code and Codex:
  - `cosky-integration` connects a Spring Boot or plain Kotlin application to a CoSky 8 server: the settings, Config import and refresh, registration and discovery, and the token from a mounted Secret.
  - `cosky-migration` moves applications and Configs from 5.x/6.x with `cosky-migrate`, and plans a cutover that switches services calling each other together.
  
  In their tests, agents with the skills met all 20 assertions, and 4 without them, inventing artifact names and property keys that 8.0 does not have. (#1284)

## Fixed

- **Copy did nothing in a Dashboard served over plain HTTP, and could lose a token just made.** Browsers give the Clipboard API only to HTTPS or localhost. Reached over plain HTTP, as through a cluster's address, every Copy button threw instead, Connect's included. There, the namespace token just made is shown only once, yet it still took one of the account's two places. Copy now works without the Clipboard API as well, says that it copied, and says to copy by hand where the browser allows no copying. (#1285)

## Upgrading from beta.9

- **A token made in Connect on beta.9 and never copied** still holds one of its account's two places. Revoke it under **Security**, on the account named like the namespace.
- Nothing else changes: the gRPC API, the protos, REST, the data in Redis and the properties. Applications stay on Spring Boot 4.2.0 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.0. `cosky-migrate` and the Dashboard come with this release.

## Known limits

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **On Sentinel,** while a master that hangs still holds the connection hints come on, each replica reads every namespace every second instead. A write then takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 30% of its CPU. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **A late Namespace creation that takes a write before it is undone** stays, without an object, and the server logs an error. That takes a write in the round trip between making the namespace and dropping it.
- **Removing every CoSky import at once** leaves their properties in place. A refresh that loaded no CoSky Config at all is not taken as one that ran the imports, so that nothing is dropped by mistake.
- **The server does not stop an account from granting itself roles** it may write; see the security guide.
